assertions.name: measured_N_power_is_cusp_independent
assertions.source: p = 3/2 fitted at both c = 1 and c = 2, agreeing to better than 1e-5 — not assumed at either

assertions.name: missing_step_is_trivial_at_c_1_and_2
assertions.source: g(2)/g(1) = 1 to ~17 digits, which excludes 2^((c-1)/2), 2^(c-1), c, sqrt(c) and c^(1/4); only g == 1 survives, so the exponent tension does not leak into the constant

assertions.name: naive_dglz_count_disagrees_at_c_equals_2
assertions.source: delta = c with a c-independent offset reproduces 3/2 at c = 1 and demands 2 at c = 2, a gap of 1/2 in the exponent — so the dictionary needs a c-dependent step that is not written down

description: Makes the c >= 2 normalisation gap concrete. DGLZ eq (2.1)/(2.2) give Z ~ N^(delta/2) with delta = h1 - h0, which for a hyperbolic manifold with c cusps at the geometric rep is delta = c — a cusp-DEPENDENT power. The corpus extracts c_sigma with a cusp-INDEPENDENT N^(-3/2), and the exponent is fitted rather than assumed (1.49999998 at c=1, 1.4999992 at c=2). The measurement is the solid side: a wrong exponent makes the limit diverge or vanish as a power of N rather than biasing it by a constant, and c_sigma(L5a1) converges to 20 digits. So a c-dependent step is missing from the dictionary between the corpus's c_sigma and DGLZ's S_1/s_1 — most plausibly in the colored-Jones normalisation for a link. This is the independent reason constants cannot be transported between the two. Derives nothing.

dglz_prediction.eq_2_2: delta(rho) = h1 - h0,  hi = dim H^i(M; E_rho)
dglz_prediction.standard_count: hyperbolic, c cusps, discrete faithful rep, adjoint coefficients: h0 = 0, h1 = c => delta = c
dglz_prediction.count_is_my_inference: DGLZ state (2.2) but do not evaluate h1 for a cusped manifold anywhere in the paper; the h1 = c count is standard but is MINE here, not theirs

exponent_is_self_certifying.why: a wrong p does not bias c_sigma by a constant — the discrepancy is a positive power of N -> infinity, so the limit diverges or vanishes instead of converging
exponent_is_self_certifying.observed: c_sigma(L5a1) converges to 20 digits at p = 3/2, so 3/2 is correct at c = 2 as a matter of measurement

bound_on_the_missing_step.model: k_measured(c) = k_true * g(c) for a missing dictionary step g
bound_on_the_missing_step.reading: every non-trivial candidate dies on the c=1 -> c=2 ratio; only g == 1 survives. So whatever fixes the exponent bookkeeping contributes exactly 1 to the CONSTANT at c = 1 and c = 2 — the tension is in the power and does not leak into k at the cusp numbers tested. This PARTLY RELIEVES the concern this probe opens with.
bound_on_the_missing_step.c3_is_not_a_cusp_law: L6a4 deviates 0.35%, but a systematic c-dependence would have shown at c = 2 and does not (17 digits). More likely specific to that computation, as its own witness says

data.what_is_missing: a c-dependent step in the dictionary between the corpus's c_sigma normalisation and DGLZ's S_1/s_1. Most plausibly the colored-Jones normalisation for a LINK: c components each coloured by N, and the eq (4.4) ratio against the solid torus. Never worked out here.
bears_on: the retraction of 'the DGLZ /2 is the corpus's k' — constants cannot be transported while this is open
the retracted 2^((c-1)/2) per-cusp factor, which lived here
L6a4's unexplained 0.35% at c = 3, which sits in the same territory
data.scope: no derivation and no new measurement. Two fitted exponents read from committed witnesses, one cohomology count that is an inference rather than a DGLZ statement, and the size of the gap.
